notes: Evertz EQX16 is a highly modular, passive-backplane routing frame (16RU main frame + separate 1RU power-supply frame) that scales from 18x18 up to 288x288 video I/O in steps of 18 via hot-swappable input/output cards; there is no single fixed port count or fixed set of labeled ports. The Video In/Out ports listed here (18 in / 18 out) represent the smallest concrete, officially orderable configuration, the "EQX16G-18X18-3G" base package (3G/HD/SD-SDI + ASI), which matches the "3G" grade shown on the datasheet's front page icons; larger configs (up to 288x288) use the same BNC connectors and formats, just more of them, and an HD-only base package (EQX16G-18X18H) exists that would be graded sdi-hd instead. Q-Link, Serial (RS-422/232 D9), Ethernet (4x RJ-45, 10/100baseT), and the 2x BNC reference inputs are fixed connectors present on every EQX16 frame controller regardless of I/O card population. Optional fiber I/O (SFP1R-2 dual optical receiver / SFP1T13-2 dual optical transmitter, LC/PC connectors, up to 3Gb/s, via the "+F" fiber rear-plate option on input cards) is available but not included in the port list since it is a non-default card option. Power: PSU modules are auto-ranging 100-240V AC (1200W per module, up to 4 load-sharing modules for 1:1 redundancy) with an external 48V DC alternative per module; the datasheet does not specify the physical AC inlet connector, so IEC (C14-style) was assumed. RS-422/232 ports use a shared D9 female connector, software-selectable per port between the two protocols. Sourced from Evertz's own product page (evertz.com/products/EQX16) and its official "EQX16 — 288x288 Enterprise Hybrid Video/Audio/IP Router" datasheet (Rev. 17-1), the latter mirrored by authorized dealer PlanetComm (planetcomm.com) — both agree on all specs extracted.
